 --> EPFO rolls out WhatsApp services, automatic settlement of inactive PF accounts up to Rs 1,000: What subscribers need to know
 Union Labour and Employment Minister Mansukh Mandaviya launched the initiative on Sunday during the celebration of EPFO's 74th Foundation Day.

 Subscribers can view passbooks and recent transactions.
 Automatic settlement introduced for inoperative accounts.

 The Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) has rolled out services through WhatsApp, allowing subscribers to check their Provident Fund (PF) balance, access passbook details and view their latest five transactions without having to visit an EPFO office.
 Union Labour and Employment Minister Mansukh Mandaviya launched the initiative on Sunday during the celebration of EPFO's 74th Foundation Day.
 Under the new facility, EPF subscribers can access their PF balance, the latest five transactions and passbook information through EPFO's verified WhatsApp service. The platform will also offer personalised guidance and assistance to members in completing requirements related to the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana (PMVBRY), according to a Labour Ministry statement.
 The initiative aims to make routine EPFO services more accessible through a familiar mobile platform and reduce the need for subscribers to visit EPFO offices for basic queries and services.
 Automatic settlement of inoperative EPF accounts

 Alongside the WhatsApp facility, Mandaviya also launched the automatic settlement of eligible inoperative EPF accounts.
 Under this initiative, subscribers with Aadhaar-verified inoperative EPF accounts carrying balances of up to Rs 1,000 will no longer need to file individual claims to withdraw their dues.
 Instead, the EPFO will initiate the settlement process automatically after completing the prescribed identity and bank account verification.
 The move is expected to facilitate the transfer of eligible amounts to their rightful beneficiaries and simplify the process of recovering small, unclaimed PF balances.
 According to the Labour Ministry, approximately one lakh accounts involving a total amount of Rs 5 crore are expected to benefit from the initiative.
 EPFO marks 74 years 
 The foundation day celebration also saw the release of seven publications highlighting the organisation's focus on knowledge creation, institutional learning, legal awareness and compassionate governance.
 Addressing the event, Mandaviya said that over its 74-year journey, the EPFO had emerged as a trusted institution for the country's workforce.
 He highlighted that the organisation had accumulated a corpus of Rs 32 lakh crore through contributions from more than 8 crore members, reflecting the trust placed in the institution and the dedication of its workforce.
 The minister urged EPFO officials to prioritise worker-centric innovations as the organisation approaches its 75th year. He also called on the workforce to adapt to changing times, build resilience and continuously improve institutional processes.
